q1_hook.why: The product box is in frame and a hand is working from the first frame (S1, H3), but nothing says what the activity is, who it is for or what it gives: no text, voice or result (H1, H2, T3). A scrolling viewer has no reason to wait, and the first change comes late (E1).

beats.what: The scribbled page held still, no hand in frame

q2_flow.why: The only hook is a late reveal: the tile at 0:23 is the first sign of a game and nothing in the first 20 s promises it (H5). Repeated scribbling and a 4 s still hold sag (R1, R3). No text or voice names the aim (T1). At 46 s it is long for one trick (R2).

q3_cta.why: No action is asked anywhere, so interest has nowhere to go: no keyword (C3), no question (C5), no named person to send it to (C4). The brand tag is the only pointer.

q4_shown.what: Top-down hands only: grey letters written on a sheet, red scribbles over them, a red translucent magnetic tile that reveals a letter, an alphabet strip with coloured discs. The marker box is in the corner from 0:00. No child, face, text or price.
q4_shown.why: The marker is used throughout and its box is visible at the start (S1, H3), but its washable claim is never stated or shown (C7). The activity is shown with no child, reaction or result, so we do not see that it works (K8, S6). Hands only keeps children off screen (S4, S5).

q5_edit.what: Hard cuts at 22.9 and 26.6 s. Time skips at about 0:05 and 0:17, where the page fills within a second. After 0:27 the view swings between page, tile and alphabet strip. No text or voice. Ends mid-action on a blue disc.
q5_edit.why: The time skips cut slow writing, as jump cuts should (E2, R1). But the 4 s still hold and 46 s length are slow for a trick first seen at 0:23 (R1, R2). With no text or voice, nothing says what to watch (E4, T1). It ends mid-action (E8).

q6_topic.what: A home letter game with markers, a red tile and an alphabet strip, for teaching letters or numbers. Serves a parent wanting a quick learning activity.
q6_topic.why: An easy activity from supplies a parent already owns is useful (K4) and could be saved (R7), but it is explained in neither words nor text, and "הילדים ממש נהנים" is only in the caption. No named concern, occasion or feeling (K6, K7, K1).

q7_filmed.what: Handheld top-down phone shots on a light wooden table in daylight, a woman's hand with red nails. Marker box in the corner at the start, later close-ups through a red tile and a letter strip with coloured discs. Drifting, tilting camera.
q7_filmed.why: Top-down hands is the first-choice view (S4, F5), with the brand box in frame at 0:00 (H3).

q8_text.on_screen: None. No headline, label, subtitle or CTA text in any frame. The only readable words are the Hebrew letters on the sheet and the strip, and the Giotto Turbo marker box in the corner from 0:00 to about 0:05.
q8_text.caption: "ערכתי לכם סרטון של". Five short lines: "פעילות סופר קלה להכין בבית", "אפשר ללמד אותיות / מספרים", "הילדים ממש נהנים!", the tag @giotto_israel. About 20 words. No hashtags, no ask, no partnership word.
q8_text.why: With no text on screen, a muted or scrolling viewer cannot tell what the activity is (T1, T3, H6). The caption gives the aim and ease but no parent keywords or hashtags (T7), and only a brand tag, no partnership word (S7, T8).

weak_points: No text, voice or CTA; the idea shows only at 0:23; 46 s with a still hold and repeated scribbling; drifting handheld; no child's reaction; the partnership only a tag.
lumebook_takeaway: Prop the phone top-down, show the finished result first with a one-line headline, cut the slow parts and end on a CTA.
